notes.title: 1.1.14 Update
notes.content:
[b]Autonomy[/b]

If you've ever felt overwhelmed keeping up with crime in Freemont, this update is for you!

This update adds a new policy called "Autonomy" that allows units to automatically respond to most calls on their own. Typically, the unit closest to the crime will respond within a few seconds of the call coming in from dispatch. 

If enabled, the policy has multiple settings to allow you to determine from how far away units should try to automatically respond.

Units will NOT automatically respond to raids, investigations, car chases, dragnets, or any call requiring the responding unit to have a certain skill level.

Once a unit has been dispatched to a call, whether automatically or by the player, the call will no longer continue to request a unit response, even if the player calls the unit away from the crime to go do something else.

By default, only traffic units are set to respond automatically, but you can configure Autonomy any way you like for all divisions from the Policies menu.

[b]Other Changes[/b]

Public Service Announcement perk now affects crime waves already in progress. If a crime wave is already happening when the perk is activated, the crime wave has its duration reduced. (The previous system only reduced the duration of the crime wave if the perk was activated before the crime wave hit.)

Reduced penalty for having crowds present at burglary and homicide investigations.

Fixed a bug that caused homicide and burglary crowds to deduct Enforcement points before the crowd had even spawned when restoring a saved game where burglaries or homicides were active.

Fixed a bug that could cause crowd members to be restored with the wrong combat system data.

Fixed an issue that would cause gang member icons to display as white rather than their appropriate gang color.

Fixed a bug that could cause lovers to get stuck in the game after completing the Bondage Cuffs call.

Fixed an issue that caused homicides to be reported too many times. At most, a homicide should now only be reported as suspicious activity, and then once more as a murder scene.

notes.title: 1.1.13 Update
notes.content:
A crowd of onlookers may now spawn around homicide and burglary investigations. The presence of these curious citizens will drive down your Enforcement score. The onlookers can be dispersed by sending units to talk to them or with the helicopter megaphone. The crowd will not interfere with the investigation itself.

Police tape now appears around homicide and burglary investigations when a unit arrives at the scene. Establishing this perimeter will encourage onlookers to leave.

The police tape system for the structure fire event has been changed to work like the new police tape system for burglaries and homicides. As soon as any unit appears at the scene, the police tape will be established.

Using the helicopter megaphone now causes the helicopter to stop moving if it was following a suspect. This will help prevent a situation where a helicopter dispatched to a crowd by clicking on a suspect would follow the suspect away from the crowd if that suspect left upon hearing the helicopter's instruction to leave the area.

Activating the Helicopter Pad perk now triggers a notification from the tip system advising the player that the helicopter still needs to be purchased at a Police Department before it can be used.

Fixed an issue that would cause the "Insufficient Funds" message to get stuck on the interface when trying to buy a helicopter without enough money to actually do so.

Fixed a bug that could cause warrants to reappear on the map for suspects who were already under arrest when restoring a game.

notes.title: 1.1.9 Update
notes.content:
This simple update re-balances the system for figuring Service approval scores.

The previous system was a lifetime score that reflected your performance over the entire course of a game. This made it different from how other scores are factored.

Now, the Service score is calculated like all the other public approval scores: A new survey runs each week and then the memory of previous successes and failures is forgotten. This makes the score more responsive to what's currently happening and makes it easier to win or lose points for Service.

notes.title: 1.1.8 Update
notes.content:
The New Game setup menu has a new feature called "Crime Curve" that allows you to determine how quickly more advanced types of crimes are allowed to start spawning in the game. The Easy setting will introduce more crime types at a much slower rate. The Hard setting will introduce them very quickly. The Medium setting will introduce them at the same rate they've always been introduced.

Hovering the mouse over a unit currently dispatched to go do something will draw a line on the screen between the unit and their destination. This is intended to make it easier for players to see which units are going where.

Stings now display their effectiveness at attracting suspects with a "Coverage" meter. Click on any sting to open its details and see the Coverage rating for that type of sting. Deploying more stings of that same type will increase their chances of attracting suspects.

Drug Lords are now much more likely to spawn.

Units going to deploy a spike strip now use lights and sirens and move faster to carry out this action.

Units currently using a spike strip now display their status as "Operating spike strip."

The Tips system can now only alert the player once about having a low cash balance.

Fixed a bug that would not send a unit to bust a suspect at a sting by clicking the unit on the undercover officer rather than the sting icon itself.

Fixed a bug that caused Captain assignment buttons to remain active in pause mode if the player's money balance dropped below the cost to assign a captain while paused.

Fixed a bug that would allow suspects who are part of a group of suspects (such as a group of three vandals) to be removed from the game while their friends were still being processed by the police.

Fixed a bug that could make it impossible to investigate some homicides.

Fixed a bug that would alert players they had units healed and waiting at the hospital before the units were actually healed when restoring a saved game.

Fixed a bug that would allow the player to spend Intelligence Points revealing the same crime over and over while the game is paused.

notes.title: 1.1.7 Update
notes.content:
The Recruiting Drive perk now has a chance to increase the skills of applicants while it is active, in addition to also reducing the time it takes to reshuffle the applicant list.

The game now features a pop-up help system that will provide players with useful advice and notifications while they play. In addition to providing help to new players, these notifications will also offer helpful reminders. You'll receive a notification if a unit is waiting for backup, if units are waiting outside the Police Academy or hospital, if an undercover unit is waiting for a marked unit to make an arrest, and so on. These notifications can be disabled from the Options menu in the Graphics/UI section.

Players can now choose to prevent the camera from automatically centering itself on whatever crime is being revealed by an informant. This feature can be enabled or disabled with the "Informant Camera" toggle from the Options menu in the Controls section.

Buttons for controlling game speed have now been added to the interface. The keyboard controls for game speed still work the same as before.

Undercover agents do not blow their cover as quickly.

Patched a very rare bug that could cause public approval meters to stop updating.

Modified four intersections around town that weren't navigable and would cause characters to take detours around them.

Fixed a bug that would cause the helicopter to continue following some moving crimes even after it was ordered to halt with the STOP button.

Fixed an issue that failed to remove units from their group when those units died. This could cause remaining units in the group to no longer be selected when selecting the group.

Fixed an issue that allowed the player to click the Specialized Gear perk again after it had already been unlocked.

Corrected a problem that would prevent the camera from zooming in or out after closing a crime details window for a case that was already closed.

Fixed a bug that caused the tutorial to get stuck if the player assigned backup to a waiting unit before being prompted by the tutorial to do so.

notes.title: Update 1.1.4 is here!
notes.content:
To: Chief of Police of Freemont

Subject: New content has arrived!

Version 1.1.4 of the game is live, and it brings with it a new Challenge mode, new crime, new perk, new features, and various tweaks and fixes.

All of this new content is detailed below, so keep reading to learn how it all works!

[b]COMMUNITY OUTREACH[/b]

This new perk allows your units to build relationships with the community they serve. You'll be able to improve relationships by sending units to engage in activities at venues that appear around town once the perk has been unlocked.

These venues will disappear for a while once they've been used, but don't worry! They'll reappear eventually so your units may continue to visit them.

Each unit's relationship with the community is rated between 1 and 5 stars. As the unit continues to improve their relationship, they'll unlock their own individual perks!

1 Star: A slightly lower chance that suspects will fight or run when dealing with the unit.

2 Stars: A slight chance that suspects will confess to carrying weapons or drugs. This is especially useful for departments that do not conduct routine searches.

3 Stars: A chance to gain additional Intelligence points when the unit arrests a suspect.

4 Stars: A greatly reduced chance that suspects will fight or run when dealing with the unit.

5 Stars: A greatly increased chance that suspects will confess to carrying weapons or drugs.

Remember, each unit has their own relationship with the community. The more units who build up their relationship, the safer everyone will be!

[b]HOUSE CLEANER CHALLENGE[/b]

A new challenge mode is included with the update that will task you with taking control of an existing police force that has been horribly mismanaged. Your objective will be to correct all of the mistakes that the previous administration made and gain control of a city that is already in chaos before time runs out.

[b]HOSTAGE-BARRICADE SITUATION[/b]

This new crime allows you to get a little more involved with police work. In this case, an armed suspect has taken hostages and locked themselves in a building. You'll need to dispatch a police negotiator to the scene to talk to them.

The police negotiator you send to this call should have a higher Interrogation skill. Once the negotiator arrives at the scene, they'll wait for your instructions. Click the crime bubble (without units selected) to see your options for negotiating with the suspect.

Your police negotiator can try to learn about the suspect using their Interrogation skill. The higher their skill, the more likely the negotiator is to discover something useful about the suspect that may help you decide what other actions to take. For instance, suspects who are hungry may want food delivered to their location. 

Taking actions that improve the suspect's cooperation will get you closer to rescuing the hostages safely. But be careful! You have a limited number of actions you can take before the suspect must be ordered to surrender. If the suspect isn't feeling particularly cooperative when ordered to surrender, they may do something drastic and endanger the hostages.

We don't want you to feel pressured to have to get involved with this crime if you're overwhelmed with other tasks whenever it pops up. It's perfectly safe to call units away from the scene to go deal with other things.

The crime will close itself automatically after ten minutes if you haven't resolved it by then.

[b]Starting Units[/b]

This is a brand new feature that allows you to begin a new game with units already hired and positioned around the city. Look for it on the main menu when setting up a new game!

Starting units do not cost you any money, so your starting funds will remain untouched.

Traffic, Investigation and SWAT will all start the game staffed with units when this feature is enabled. It may be a good idea to check their skills and send them to training if you aren't satisfied with them.

[b]New Music[/b]

This update brings 3 new music tracks to the game! These tracks add an additional 11 minutes of music to the game.

Owners of the game's Original Soundtrack on Steam will see that product update automatically to include these new tracks soon.

[b]New Achievements[/b]

This update introduces 4 new achievements to go with our new features.

House Cleaner: This achievement unlocks when you beat the House Cleaner challenge.

My Hero: This achievement unlocks when you rescue hostages safely from a Hostage-Barricade Situation.

A Friend Indeed: This achievement unlocks when you max out a unit's community relationship.

In It Together: This achievement unlocks when you max out community relationships for 10 units in a single game.

[b]ADDITIONAL CHANGES AND FIXES[/b]

Assaults are now much more likely to occur.

Stings can now be properly placed while the game is paused.

Fixed a bug that allowed some moving crimes (like reckless driving) to continue to move while being arrested.

Fixed a bug that could cause runaways to get stuck in the game when closing their case manually.

Fixed a bug that allowed units to continue investigating a runaway after the runaway reached 18 years of age.

Fixed an issue that caused the Police Department Menu to not flag insufficient skills for investigators and SWAT.

Fixed a bug that allowed units to be fired while they're in training.

Fixed a problem with the Patrol Manager that caused the game to ignore keyboard input after the patrols window was closed by pressing Escape.

Fixed a bug that could cause crime bubbles to pop up larger than they should be when running the game at certain resolutions.

notes.title: New content update coming soon!
notes.content:
To: Chief of Police of Freemont

Subject: New content coming soon

We're excited about a brand new update coming to JURISDICTION, and we'd like to take a moment to tell you what you can expect to see!

Read on to learn more about our new features and changes coming soon to the game.

[b]COMMUNITY OUTREACH[/b]

This is a perk you'll be able to unlock within the Annual Report that will enable your officers to start building relationships with the community they serve. Cops can stop by the diner to order a sandwich, they can volunteer at the local animal shelter, they can challenge the locals to a competitive game at the arcade, or they just discuss their favorite literature at the bookstore. Every interaction improves the unit's community relationship.

Every time a unit levels up their community relationship, they unlock a new unit perk for themselves that will improve their interactions with suspects. These unit perks do things like reducing the chances that a suspect will run or fight when stopped by that unit, or persuading suspects to voluntarily confess to carrying weapons or drugs.

[b]HOUSE CLEANER CHALLENGE[/b]

A new challenge mode will be included with the update that will task you with taking control of an existing police force that's been horribly mismanaged. Your objective will be to correct all of the mistakes that the previous administration made and gain control of a city that's already in chaos before time runs out.

[b]HOSTAGE-BARRICADE SITUATION[/b]

This is a new crime in which a suspect will take people hostage and barricade themselves in a building. You'll need to dispatch a unit with excellent Interrogation skill to act as a negotiator if you want to get the hostages out safely. But this isn't just another crime where you dispatch a unit and then sit back while they do the rest.

We wanted to add a crime to the game where you get to be a little more involved, and in this case, you'll be in charge of directing the interactions between your negotiator and the suspect.

The choices you make could lead the suspect to release the hostages and surrender peacefully, or you might inadvertently provoke the suspect to do something drastic.

[b]PRE-MADE UNITS[/b]

If you prefer not to have to build your police force from the ground up every time you start a new game, this feature is for you!

When starting a new game, you'll have the option to launch with a selection of units already hired and positioned around the city. These units will not cost you anything, leaving your starting funds untouched.

[b]OTHER ITEMS[/b]

A handful of smaller items will be included in this update, including new achievements, new music tracks and some bug fixes. 

Owners of the game's Original Soundtrack on Steam will see that their soundtrack will be updated to include the new music soon after the game update is live.

[b]CONCLUSION[/b]

We'll provide more information about these features and explain the fine details of how they work in another announcement once the update goes live. We're excited about this upcoming content, and we hope you are too!

This update will be available within the next couple of weeks.

Over and out!

notes.title: 1.0.2 Update
notes.content:
Camera can now be moved while the game is paused.

Suspects committing a moving crime (such as speeding or car theft) who run from the cops will now remain visible until they reach the map edge. This fixes a situation where cops in pursuit of that suspect would give up the chase if the suspect moved out of range and disappeared even though their crime bubble was still visible.

The system for calculating arrest ratios has been modified to include suspects who are downed by police during combat. This makes it much easier to maintain a good Enforcement score so long as the player is responding to crimes and attempting to arrest suspects, even if those suspects choose to fight and lose.

Suspects who haven't committed a crime yet, but who run from the police, can now be stopped and arrested properly.

Added an icon for "evasion" that will display along with all the other conviction icons that pop up above suspects being arrested.

Fixed a bug that would cause cops to try to pursue stopped suspects rather than provide backup to the arresting officer when attempting to assign backup by clicking the suspect.

Fixed a bug that could prevent some suspects from being pulled over if they were discovered headed for their escape after leaving a crime scene.

Fixed a bug that caused the helicopter to not move to certain crimes.

Fixed a bug that could cause the Annual Report to fail to reset the count of unreasonable searches for the new year.

Reduced frequency at which newspapers can report on unreasonable searches.

tags.feature: Camera can now be moved while the game is paused.

tags.bug: Suspects committing a moving crime (such as speeding or car theft) who run from the cops will now remain visible until they reach the map edge. This fixes a situation where cops in pursuit of that suspect would give up the chase if the suspect moved out of range and disappeared even though their crime bubble was still visible.

tags.balance_change: The system for calculating arrest ratios has been modified to include suspects who are downed by police during combat. This makes it much easier to maintain a good Enforcement score so long as the player is responding to crimes and attempting to arrest suspects, even if those suspects choose to fight and lose.

tags.bug: Suspects who haven't committed a crime yet, but who run from the police, can now be stopped and arrested properly.

tags.feature: Added an icon for "evasion" that will display along with all the other conviction icons that pop up above suspects being arrested.

tags.bug: Fixed a bug that would cause cops to try to pursue stopped suspects rather than provide backup to the arresting officer when attempting to assign backup by clicking the suspect.

Fixed a bug that caused the helicopter to not move to certain crimes.
Fixed a bug that could cause the Annual Report to fail to reset the count of unreasonable searches for the new year.

notes.title: 1.0.1 Update
notes.content:
Added support for additional aspect ratios and resolutions, including 3440 x 1440.

Fixed a bug that allowed the player to use the Forensics Outsourcing perk without being charged for it when restarting investigations.

Various fixes and tweaks to the UI to make it scale better with resolution changes.

Certain item previews on the PD Menu now use higher resolution images for better quality.

Fixed a bug that could cause item previews to get stuck on the PD menu for Investigators.

Fixed a bug that stopped edge scrolling from working when the mouse would move to the bottom of the screen.

Fixed a bug that could cause certain suspects to get stuck in the game after being killed.

Fixed a bug that would cause the game to forget the user's preference for autosaving if the user disabled autosaving.
